reason: The text fragment is primarily a narrative from the Book of Judges (chapters 13-16) focusing on the birth, life, and exploits of Samson. While the opening mentions that the Israelites 'continued to do evil in the eyes of the Lord,' the main body consists of Samson's story—his miraculous birth, his encounters with the Philistines, his marriage, and the Delilah incident. The only scene involving dialogue from Israelite leadership (the men of Judah) occurs when they question the Philistines' invasion ('Why have you come up against us?') and subsequently bind Samson to appease the Philistines. This represents compliance with foreign rule rather than complaint against their own leaders. No passage in this text shows the Hebrew people explicitly complaining about or criticizing their leaders.
